This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual/Physical Mode).
2.
Since these two criminal appeals arise out of one and same case record, the same are heard together and disposed of by this common order with the consent of the learned counsels for the parties.

3. These appeals U/S. 101 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 (in short "the Act") are directed against the orders dated 25.06.2024 & 06.07.2024 passed in Special G.R. Case No.07/5 of 2024 arising out of Bisra P.S. Case No. 39 of 2024.

entities.text: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015

sentences.text:
By the aforesaid two orders, the learned Additional District Judge-cum-Children's Court,
Sundargarh has turned down the prayer for bail of each of the appellants-CICLs for commission of offences punishable Under Sections 376(D)/323/506/201 of the IPC, r/w. Section 6 of POCSO Act and Sections 3(1)(r)/3(1)(w)(i)/3(1)(w)(ii)/3(2)(v)/3(2)(vi) of the SC & ST (PoA) Act and 66-E of the IT Act, on the main allegation of committing rape upon the victim and blackmailing her by taking advantage of her caste.
4.

Heard, Mr. Sougat Dash, learned counsel for the appellants-CICLs appearing virtually from Sambalpur, Mr. B.K. Behera, learned counsel for the informant and Mr. T.K. Praharaj, learned Standing Counsel in the matter and perused the record.

sentences.text: At the outset, Mr. Sougat Dash, learned counsel for the appellants-CICLs by taking this Court through the photocopy of the certified copy of the deposition of the victim-PW.1 in ST Case No.07/10 of 2024 which is taken on record submits that nothing has been stated by the victim against the present appellants-CICLs in the trial of the case against adult accused and thereby, the present appellants-CICLs having detained in observation home since 15.02.2024, no fruitful purpose would be served by their further detention in observation home.

On the other hand, Mr.
Behera did not raise any serious objection to the prayer of the Appellants for grant of bail.

On the contrary, Mr. Prahraj seriously opposes the prayer of the Appellants by contending inter-alia that since co-accused is an adult, the release of the Appellants-CICLs on bail would bring them into the association of such adult accused and thereby, there is every likelihood of exposure of the Appellants to moral and psychological danger by their release on bail. Perused, the photocopy of the certified copy of deposition of the victim as produced.

6. After having considered the rival submissions and taking into account the nature and gravity of the offences as alleged against the Appellants vis--vis the accusations sought to be brought against them and regard being had to the evidence of the victim in the case against the adult accused together with the observation made in Social Investigation Report as produced by Mr. T.K. Praharaj,
learned Standing Counsel which is taken on record and last but not the least, taking into account the detention of the appellants-CICLs in observation home since 15.02.2024 and further taking into account the principle that bail should not be refused to the juvenile, unless the grounds of proviso to Section 12 of the Act are satisfied, which has not been met out in this case, this Court admits each of the appellants-CICLs to bail.

Hence, both the criminal appeals stand allowed and the order impugned in these appeals are,
hereby, set aside.
Consequently, the appellants-CICLs are directed to be released on bail on such terms and conditions as deems fit and proper by the learned Court in seisin over the matter.
7. Accordingly, both the CRLAs stand disposed of.
